name: RT9361AGE
title: RT9361A/B: regulated inductorless charge pump, fixed 5 V or 4.5 V output
summary: The RT9361A/B is a switched-capacitor DC/DC converter that steps a 2.8 V-to-VOUT input up to a regulated fixed output: 5 V for the RT9361A, 4.5 V for the RT9361B. It needs three capacitors (input, output and one flying capacitor) and no inductor, and runs from a 1 MHz oscillator. Soft start limits the inrush at start-up and on mode changes; current limiting and short-circuit protection are built in, and quiescent current is 2 mA typical with 0.1 µA in shutdown. The RT9361A delivers at least 110 mA and the RT9361B at least 150 mA above 3.2 V input. It comes in SOT-23-6, TSOT-23-6 and WDFN-6L 2x2; the RT9361AGE is the 5 V version in SOT-23-6, halogen-free.

Every version is RoHS compliant, compatible with IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020, and suited to SnPb and Pb-free soldering.

circuits.title: Typical application: three white LEDs
circuits.description: The input source charges CIN at VIN; CPUMP sits between CP and CN as the flying capacitor; COUT holds the regulated output. Three LEDs, each with its own series resistor R, hang from VOUT to ground. EN is brought out as a control input. The input may be 2.8 V up to VOUT. The capacitor values follow the load: for the RT9361A, 1 or 2.2 µF in and out with 0.22 µF flying below 60 mA, and 10 µF / 1 µF / 10 µF below 110 mA; for the RT9361B the same pairs cover 80 mA and 150 mA (VIN above 3.2 V).

circuits.title: Backlight dimming
circuits.description: Three backlight LEDs at 20 mA each, every one fed from VOUT through its own 100 Ω resistor. CIN and COUT are 2.2 µF and the flying capacitor 0.22 µF. The dimming waveforms at VIN = 3.7 V are measured on this circuit.

circuits.title: Flash LEDs
circuits.description: Camera-flash LEDs, three in parallel, each behind a resistor R from VOUT, with the output marked 4.5 V at 150 mA. CIN and COUT are 2.2 µF and CPUMP 0.22 µF.

circuits.title: Constant load
circuits.description: A 5 V, 110 mA supply for a steady load. CIN is 10 µF, CPUMP 1 µF and COUT 10 µF; a 1 µH inductor and a 1 µF capacitor to ground follow COUT before the output terminal.

circuits.title: Two devices in parallel for twice the output current
circuits.description: Two RT9361A/B share one input, one enable line and one output, giving 5 V at 180 mA from a 3.3 V input. Each device has its own 0.22 µF flying capacitor; a single 10 µF CIN and a single 10 µF COUT serve both.

equations.name: Efficiency
equations.expr: Efficiency (%) = POUT / PIN × 100 = (VOUT × IOUT) / (VIN × 2 × IOUT) × 100 = VOUT / (2 × VIN) × 100

where.IOUT: output current; in 2× mode the input current is twice IOUT

equations.note: Holds for the 2× charge-pump mode and ignores switching losses and quiescent current. At VOUT = 5 V and VIN = 3 V it gives 83.33 %; 82.72 % is measured.

equations.name: Maximum power dissipation

where.θJA: junction-to-ambient thermal resistance: 250°C/W for T/SOT-23-6, 165°C/W for WDFN-6L 2x2 (JEDEC 51-3 single-layer board)

equations.note: At TA = 25°C: (125°C − 25°C) / 250°C/W = 0.4W for T/SOT-23-6 and (125°C − 25°C) / 165°C/W = 0.606W for WDFN-6L 2x2. The allowed dissipation falls linearly to zero at 125°C ambient.

operation.text: A switched-capacitor converter with one flying capacitor between CP and CN, regulating a fixed 5 V (A) or 4.5 V (B) output. No inductor is used. The input range runs from 2.8 V up to the output voltage. Quiescent current is 2 mA typical.

The functional block diagram holds a 1 MHz oscillator controlled from EN, a switch array to CP and CN, an amplifier comparing a divided-down output against VREF, a voltage reference, current bias, a load-disconnect block and short-circuit protection.
An internal soft start holds down the inrush current both at power-up and when the converter changes mode.
EN is active high: 1.5 V or more turns the converter on, 0.4 V or less turns it off. In shutdown the supply draw is 0.1 µA typical, 1 µA maximum (VIN = 4.5 V).
Over-current protection trips between 250 mA and 500 mA (350 mA typical). With the output shorted the current is held to 60 mA typical, 90 mA maximum.

The three capacitors affect the VOUT ramp-up time, the output ripple and the transient response. Low-ESR ceramics (below 100 mΩ, X5R or X7R) perform best; low-ESR tantalum is usable with poorer ripple, and aluminium electrolytics are unsuitable because of their high ESR. CIN and COUT range from 1 µF at light load to 10 µF at heavy load (under 110 mA), CPUMP from 0.22 µF to 1 µF; at 60 mA or less, 2.2 µF for CIN and COUT with 0.22 µF for CPUMP is enough. COUT scales with CPUMP to hold ripple, and CIN and COUT stay near ten times CPUMP. Smaller values give a faster VOUT ramp-up and more ripple.

Efficiency depends on the output version, the input voltage, the load and the operating mode. In the 2× mode the input current is twice the output current, so efficiency is about VOUT / (2 × VIN): 83.33 % in theory for 5 V out from 3 V in, against 82.72 % measured.

Allowed dissipation is set by the package thermal resistance, the board, the airflow and the junction-to-ambient temperature difference, with the junction held to 125 °C. On the JEDEC 51-3 single-layer board, θJA is 250 °C/W for T/SOT-23-6 and 165 °C/W for WDFN-6L 2x2.

Switching at high frequency drives large pulsed currents in VIN and VOUT. Keep every external part as close to the IC as it will go, put a solid ground plane on the bottom layer, and join the grounds of CIN and COUT to each other right at the IC.
